A new way to run the yard

You already know your yard better than anyone. It is time your software finally caught up.

Yardsmith gives every yard, and everyone working in it, one clear picture of the day. Built around real people, not a fixed org chart.

The problem

The whiteboard remembers less than everyone assumes it does.

A whiteboard in the tack room, a group chat nobody has time to scroll back through, a paper diary for the arena. It holds together, mostly, until two horses are booked into the same arena at once, or an owner calls to ask why nobody turned her horse out.

Every person in the yard works from a slightly different picture of the same day. Those small gaps are what turn into missed turnout, double bookings, and messages that arrive too late to matter.

The turn

You did not build this yard to spend your mornings solving the same small mystery again and again.

There is a way to see the whole place clearly, all at once, without adding yet another app that only manages half the problem.

What Yardsmith is

One place that finally sees the yard the way you do.

Yardsmith brings together the physical side of the yard, which paddocks, arenas and horse walkers are free right now, with the human side, the tasks, the messages, and a clear view for owners of what is happening with their own horse.

Built by people who know a yard does not run on software, it runs on horses and the people looking after them. Yardsmith just gives everyone the same honest picture of the day.

How it works

Every yard builds its own team. Yardsmith adapts to whoever is on it.

No two yards are staffed the same way. A small livery yard might run on two people. A sport stable might have a manager, several grooms, a trainer, and a vet or farrier who visits on schedule. Roles and permissions are set up per yard, not fixed by us.

Any role you need

Real-time visibility

Every paddock, arena and walker shows what is actually true right now.

Tasks that stay clear

Each person's day is laid out for them, in order, without a scrolling chat.

A window for owners

Owners see their own horse's day, without picking up the phone.

What changes

A yard that runs on what is true, not on what someone remembers.

Nothing dramatic. The small frictions simply stop. The arena gets booked before two people show up for it at once. A new hire knows what to do without asking around. An owner checks her phone instead of calling.

What is left is more time for the part of the job that needed a person all along, the horses, and the people who show up for them every day.

Built for the way you work

Every yard is a little different. Yardsmith is built to bend around that.

One core, five directions. Yardsmith starts from the same foundation and grows into whichever shape your yard actually needs.

For partners and investors
